headline: Profit surges on record volumes and stronger realized prices
summary_short: EOG Resources posted Q2 2026 revenue of $8,620M (+57.4% y/y, +24.5% q/q) and diluted EPS of $5.15 (+109.3% y/y), as composite realized crude prices rose to $98.15/Bbl and total output hit a record 1,410.4 MBoed.
summary_long: Revenue rose 57.4% y/y and 24.5% q/q to $8,620M on higher composite crude realizations ($98.15/Bbl vs $72.47 1Q26, $64.82 2Q25) and record output of 1,410.4 MBoed. Diluted EPS of $5.15 was up 109.3% y/y; EOG's own EPS bridge attributes the $1.45 q/q gain to +$1.57 from realized prices and +$0.14 from volumes, partly offset by -$0.07 from higher per-Boe operating costs and -$0.11 from a smaller mark-to-market derivative gain ($40M vs $113M 1Q26). Cash fell 5.9% y/y to $4,907M after $1,299M of buybacks and $1.02/share dividends this quarter; long-term debt remains elevated at $7,899M versus $3,458M a year ago, reflecting the 2025 Encino acquisition financing.

drivers.explanation: EOG's own supplemental release decomposes the $1.45 q/q rise in diluted EPS ($3.70 to $5.15): +$1.57 from higher realized prices, +$0.14 from higher volumes, -$0.07 from higher operating costs per Boe, and -$0.11 from a smaller mark-to-market derivative gain.
Composite realized oil price rose to $98.15/Bbl from $72.47 in 1Q26 and $64.82 in 2Q25, while total volumes reached a record 1,410.4 MBoed, up from 1,383.8 MBoed q/q.
Gross profit growth reflects the same revenue-outpacing-costs dynamic as operating income, on higher realized prices and record volumes.
Operating income rose in line with the revenue increase from higher realized prices and volumes, as total operating expenses grew only 17.9% q/q ($4,323M to $5,092M) versus revenue's 24.5% q/q gain.
Mirrors the Operating income move; both track the same q/q swing from higher realized prices and volumes against slower-growing operating costs.
EBITDA growth mirrors the operating-income and revenue gains, adding back DD&A ($1,259M vs $1,193M q/q) which grew slower than revenue.
Net income growth mirrors the diluted-EPS bridge: higher realized prices and volumes outweighed increased operating costs and a smaller derivative mark-to-market gain versus 1Q26.
Mirrors the diluted-EPS bridge above; basic EPS rose to $5.18 from $3.72 q/q on the same price, volume, cost, and derivative dynamics.

Per the release's own EPS walk, realized-price gains added $1.57 and volume growth added $0.14 to diluted EPS q/q, partly offset by -$0.07 from higher operating costs and -$0.11 from a smaller derivative mark-to-market gain.
